actmap.name: Name of the activity. See SetAction(). Max 30 characters.
actmap.procedure: Internal standard procedure. See Procedures. Max 30 characters.
actmap.directions: Number of animation directions. Animation directions are arranged vertically in Graphics.png.
actmap.flipDir: If nonzero, this value specifies the first animation phase that is produced by mirroring one of the previous animation directions. If this value is 1, graphics of direction 1 (DIR_Right) will be drawn as a horizontally mirrored graphics of direction 0 (DIR_Left) (see clonks). If it is 7, any directions n >= 7 will be drawn using the mirrored graphics of directions 6 - n, i.e. higher direction values will be drawn using the mirrored graphics in reverse orders (cf. banner in the knights pack).
actmap.length: Number of animation phases for this activity (arranged horizontally in Graphics.png)
actmap.reverse: 0 or 1. If 1, the animation phases will be shown in reverse order.
actmap.delay: Time difference in frames (ticks) between two animation phases.
actmap.attach: Attachment to surfaces: CNAT Value, e.g. value 8 if the object should attach to the floor like a walking clonk does; or 4 for attachment to the ceiling like a hangling clonk. Only evaluated if the procedure is NONE.
actmap.facet: Animation graphics: Target rectangle from Graphics.png relative to upper left corner of unrotated object shape.
actmap.facetBase: 0 or 1. If 1, the default facet (i.e., the facet shown if the object has no action) will be drawn behind the action facet.
actmap.facetTopFace: 0 or 1. If 1, the TopFace (see DefCore.txt) will be drawn using the animated facet.
actmap.facetTargetStretch: 0 or 1. If 1, the graphics will be stretched down towards the upper border of the ActionTarget. Used e.g. for the elevator line.
actmap.nextAction: Next action being set after the current one has reached its end. Max 30 characters.
actmap.noOtherAction: 0 or 1. If 1, no other action can be set after this one (used e.g. for death or destruction). Max 30 characters.
actmap.startCall: Object script function which is called when the activity is started. Max 30 characters.
actmap.endCall: Called when an activity reaches the end of its animation. Max 30 characters.
actmap.phaseCall: Called whenever the animation phase changes. Max 30 characters.
actmap.abortCall: Called if an activity is being replaced by another before its regular end; i.e. not by a transition through NextAction. Max 30 characters.
actmap.inLiquidAction: Action to be set if the object plunges into water. Max 30 characters.
actmap.sound: Permanent sound being played during this action. Max 30 characters.
actmap.objectDisabled: 0 or 1. Restricted control of the object during this action.
actmap.digFree: Area that is dug free during this action. If 1, the area covered by the object shape is freed (like the elevator case); otherwise, the value is taken as the radius of a circular area (like a digging Clonk).
actmap.energyUsage: Energy required for this action. Normal machines should use about 500.

head.icon: Default icon for the scenario. See the scenario options in the menu system
head.title: Title for the scenario. Entries in Title.txt will override this value. Max 512 characters
head.version: Engine version required by the scenario
head.roundOptions: 0 or 1. Allow other players to change scenario properties in the menu system
head.noInitialize: 0 or 1. If 1, basic startup objects as defined in Scenario.txt (player material and buildings, animals, vegetation) are not placed. This flag is automatically set in savegaes and is used to avoid duplication by repeated scenario initialization. The flag ignores among others the values Buildings, Vehicles, Material, Vegetation, InEarth, and Animals.
head.missionAcces: The scenario will only load if the player gained this password in another scenario. See script function GainMissionAccess().
head.replay: Set automatically be the engine. Marks the scenario as record.
head.film: 0 or 1 und only valid for records. If 1, the view always follows the first player and all player controls are invisible.
head.forcedGfxMode: 0-2. 0: All engines possible; 1: NewGfx only (OpenGL/D3D); 2: OldGfx only (8bit-DDraw)

game.valueOverloads: List of definitions for which the values should be overridden. The amount will be the new value.
game.foWColor: Color of the fog of war
game.elimination: Obsolete. Player elimination by: 0 Loss of captain, 1 Loss of crew, 2 Loss of flag.
game.cooperativeGoal: Obsolete. Value for goal in the menu system (0-4)
game.createObjects: Obsolete. Game goal: These objects must be created.
game.clearObjects: Obsolete. Game goal: The object counts must be reduced to x
game.clearMaterials: Obsolete. Game goal: The material count must be reduced to x
game.baseFunctionality:
A bit mask that defines which functionality a home base object will offer. See Homebase Functionality.

Since CR.
game.baseRegenerateEnergyPrice:
The cost of recharging a clonk to 100% life energy in the home base. Default is 5. Value 0 will yield free recharging.

Since CR.

playerX.position: Start position as coordinates for the un-zoomed landscape. Both -1: Random position.
playerX.crew: Type and count of initial crew members.
playerX.knowledge: Objects the player should initially be able to create.
playerX.homeBaseMaterial: Materials available to buy at game start.
playerX.homeBaseProduction: Additional supply of materials to buy.
playerX.magic: Available spells. If the list is empty, all spells are available (backwards compatibility).

landscape.inEarth: Types and proportionate shares of buried objects.
landscape.sky: Sky texture from Graphics.c4g (without filename extension)
landscape.skyFade: Sky color gradient (RGB to RGB). Values 0-255. With all values 0, the default blue background will be used.
landscape.bottomOpen: 0 or 1. Determines wether the bottom of the game world should be open.
landscape.topOpen: 0 or 1. Determines wether the top of the game world should be open.
landscape.leftOpen: Height until which the left side of the game world is open.
landscape.rightOpen: Height until which the right side of the game world is open.
landscape.autoScanSideOpen: 0 or 1. If 1, LeftOpen and RightOpen will be set automatically depending on the landscape at game start.
landscape.mapWidth: Base width of the dynamic map.
landscape.mapHeight: Base height of the dynamic map.
landscape.mapZoom: Factor for zooming the map to the real game world. Default is 10.
landscape.amplitude: 0-100 with tolerance. Hill height for dynamic maps.
landscape.phase: 0-100 with tolerance. Hill offset for dynamic maps.
landscape.period: 0-100 with tolerance. Hill interval for dynamic maps.
landscape.random: 0-100 with tolerance. Random deviance for dynamic maps.
landscape.material: Material-texture definition of the base material for dynamic maps.
landscape.liquid: Material-texture definition of the liquid material for dynamic maps.
landscape.liquidLevel: 0-100 with tolerance. Liquid level for dynamic maps.
landscape.mapPlayerExtend: 0 or 1. Determines wether the dynamic map will be extended for every player activated at game start.
landscape.layers: Additional material layers in earth for dynamic maps.
landscape.exactLandscape: 0 or 1. Specifies wether the Landscape.bmp is an actual game landscape.
landscape.noScan: 0 or 1. If 1, some ingame landscape checks will be turned of, such as freezing, melting or material counting.
landscape.keepMapCreator: 0 or 1. If 1, the internal MapCreater won't unload after game start, so functions like DrawDefMap still work.
landscape.skyScrollMode: 0 to 2. 0: Static sky, 1: The sky moves with the wind, 2: The sky is drawn half-parallax.
landscape.foWRes: Granularity of the Fog of War. Default: 64. Warning: smaller values will improve the looks of the FoW but will also severely increase processing times.

weather.climate: 0-100 with tolerance. Average temperature. 0 warm, 100 cold.
weather.startSeason: 0-100 with tolerance. Season at game start.
weather.yearSpeed: 0-100 with tolerance. Speed of season change.
weather.wind: -100-100 with tolerance. Wind direction and strength.
weather.noGamma: 0 or 1. If 1, the current season won't cause a small global color change.

environment.objects: Environment control objects that are placed at game start.

definitions.localOnly: If LocalOnly is 1, only definitions local to the scenario file will be load.
definitions.definitionX: With Definitionx entries you can specify which object definition packs (c4d) are to be loaded with this scenario. The specified files must be available in the Clonk directory. If files are specified here, manual pack selection in the menu system is disabled.
definitions.skipDefs: List of object definitions (C4IDs) which are not to be loaded with this scenario. This can be used to prevent researching certain object types in the game.

defcore.version: Minimal engine version required by the object. Should be always the current engine version at the time of the last change.
defcore.name: Name of the object. Will be overwritten by the applicable one in the Names.txt.
defcore.category: Category of the object. Also see object categories.
defcore.maxUserSelect: Maximal allowed count when placed in the menu system.
defcore.timerCall: Regularly called timer function in the object script.
defcore.timer: Time interval between TimerCalls in frames. Default is 35.
defcore.contactCalls: 0 or 1. If 1, Contactcalls are called in the object script.
defcore.offset: Coordinate offset of the top left corner to the object center.
defcore.value: Value of the object in money points.
defcore.mass: Weight of the object. Rock 10, clonk 50, hut 1000, castle 10000.
defcore.components: Elements from which the object is composed. Uncompleted or half grown objects will only have the respective fraction of the components.
defcore.solidMask: Solid areas of the object. Target rectangle from the source graphics onto the object.
defcore.topFace: Covering layer of the object graphics. Target rectangle from the source graphics onto the object.
defcore.picture: Representative image of the object. Rectangle from the source graphics.
defcore.vertices: Number of vertices of the object. 1 to 30.
defcore.vertexX: List of horizontal vertex coordinates of the object. See vertices.
defcore.vertexY: List of vertical coordinates of the object vertices.
defcore.vertexCNAT: List of direction indicators of the object vertices. See CNAT.
defcore.vertexFriction: List of friction values of the object vertices, each 1 to 100.
defcore.entrance: Position of the entrance region relative to the object centre.
defcore.collection: Position of the intake region relative to the object centre.
defcore.collectionLimit: How many objects can be collected, or 0 for no limitation.
defcore.fireTop: Flame distance to the object's bottom line.
defcore.placement: Placement: 0 land surface, 1 in liquid, 2 in mid-air.
defcore.exclusive: 0 or 1. Determines whether the object blocks objects behind it.
defcore.contactIncinerate: Probability of incineration by contact: 0 none, or 1 (high) to 5 (low).
defcore.blastIncinerate: Incineration by explosion: 0 none, otherwise the damage level of incineration.
defcore.base: 0 or 1. Determines whether the building can be a home base.
defcore.line: 1 energy line, 2 source pipe, 3 drain pipe.
defcore.lineConnect: Connection behaviour for lines. See LineConnect.
defcore.prey: 0 or 1. Determines whether the object is prey for certain animals.
defcore.edible: 0 or 1. Determines whether the object is edible.
defcore.crewMember: 0 or 1. If 1, the object is added to the player's crew upon purchase. Objects created using CreateObject have to be added to a player's crew manually using MakeCrewMember.
defcore.growth: Growth of the object. Trees 1-4, living beings 15.
defcore.rebuy: 0 or 1. Determines whether the object can be bought back after selling it.
defcore.construction: 0 or 1. Determines whether the object can be built.
defcore.grab: 0 no grabbing, 1 grab and push, 2 grab only.
defcore.grabPutGet: Bit mask: bit 0 (value 1) putting possible, bit 1 (value 2) getting possible.
defcore.collectible: 0 or 1. Determines whether the object can be collected.
defcore.rotate: 0 no rotation, 1 full rotation, 2-360 limited rotation.
defcore.chop: 0 or 1. Determines whether the object can be chopped.
defcore.float: Floatation in liquids: 0 no floatation, otherwise floatation height above the object center.
defcore.containBlast: 0 or 1. Determines whether explosions in the object's contents affect other objects outside.
defcore.colorByOwner: 0 or 1. If 1, the specified sections of the object's graphcis are colored by the player color.
defcore.colorByMaterial: The object is colored by the color of the specified material.
defcore.horizontalFix: 0 or 1. If 1, the object can only move vertically.
defcore.borderBound: Bit mask: bit 0 (value 1) stop at the sides, bit 1 (value 2) stop at the top, bit 2 (value 4) stop at the bottom.
defcore.uprightAttach: If not 0, the unrotated object attaches to solid areas (attachment directions 8-10).
defcore.stretchGrowth: 0 or 1. If 1, the uncomplete object (see GetCon) is scaled, not sliced from the bottom like a construction site.
defcore.basement: 0 no basement, 1 normal basement, other values reserved.
defcore.noBurnDecay: 0 or 1. If 1, the object does not decompose if burning.
defcore.incompleteActivity: 0 or 1. If 1, the object can have activities set even if it's not complete.
defcore.oversize: 0 or 1. The object can be scaled over 100% using DoCon.
defcore.fragile: 0 or 1. The object should not be thrown.
defcore.noPushEnter: 0 or 1. The object can not be pushed into another object's entrance (e.g. elevator case).
defcore.vehicleControl: Bit mask: bit 0 (value 1) object can be controlled by grabbing from the outside and/or bit 1 (value 2) from the inside. With active VehicleControl, clonk orders (commands) are also passed to the grabbed object as ControlCommand calls and can be processed and/or overloaded by the controlled object's script. See Control-Funktionen.
defcore.pathfinder: 1 - 10. Determines search depth of the pathfinder algorithm (default 1). Warning: higher values may slow down the game. By setting this value you can also enable non-CrewMember objects to use pathfinding when executing commands.
defcore.noComponentMass: 0 or 1. If 1, the object's contents is not added to the object's total mass. This can be used to prevent small container objects from turning into killer throwing items.
defcore.noStabilize: 0 or 1. If 1, the object will not straighten itself to 0° if within a certain upright range.
defcore.closedContainer: 0 or 1. If 1, clonks inside this object can not lighten the Fog of War outside.
defcore.silentCommands: 0 or 1. Can be used to prevent failure messages caused by failed commands.
defcore.noBurnDamage: 0 or 1. If 1, the object does not take damage when burning.
defcore.temporaryCrew: 0 or 1. If 1, the object is not stored in the permanent crew of a player.
defcore.smokeRate: 0 to 200: determines the amount of smoke caused by the burning object. 0 for no smoke, 100 is default. If other than 0, the object will always generate maximum smoke when traveling at high velocity (e.g. a fire arrow).
defcore.noBreath: 0 or 1. If 1, the object does not need oxygen, even if it's a living being.
defcore.conSizeOff: Values grater than 0 are deducted from the top of necessary construction space.
defcore.noSell: 0 or 1. If 1 the object can not be sold.
defcore.noGet: 0 or 1. If 1 the object can not be taken from containers by a clonk.
defcore.noFight: 0 or 1. If 1 the object will never enter into a fight with other living beings.
defcore.liftTop: If an object with Action procedure "LIFT" lifts its target to this value above object center the function LiftTop is called in the object script.
defcore.rotatedEntrance: 0 entrance is open if the object is upright only; 1 entrance is always open; 2-360 entrance is open within the specified object rotation in degrees. From 4.95.4.
defcore.moveToRange: Maximum range at which the waypoint of a movement command can be touched for a successful hit. Default value 5. From 4.95.4.
defcore.noTransferZones: 0 or 1. If 1 the object's pathfinding will ignore any transfer zones. From 4.95.4.
defcore.autoContextMenu: 0 or 1. If 1, the building's context menu will open automatically upon entry. From 4.9.7.7.

physical.canConstruct: 0 or 1. Construct. If greater than 1, percentage construction speed. (100 normal, 50 half, etc.)
physical.corrosionResist: 0 or 1. Determines wether the object resists acid.
physical.breatheWater: 0 object breathes air, 1 object breathes water.

particle.name: Name of the particle definition. This name is also used to refer to this particle type in scripts. For multi-language display in the menu system you should use the Names.txt component.
particle.maxCount: Maximum number of instances of this particle type. See instance control.
particle.minLifetime: Only for smoke particles: lower limit for the lifetime, which ranges from MinLifetime to MaxLifetime.
particle.maxLifetime: Only for smoke particles: upper limit for the lifetime, which ranges from MinLifetime to MaxLifetime.
particle.initFn: Identifier for the function used to initialize the particle. For valid functions see section particle functions.
particle.execFn: Identifier for the function used to execute the particle each frame. For valid functions see section particle functions.
particle.drawFn: Identifier for the function used to draw the particle. For valid functions see section drawing functions.
particle.collisionFn: Identifier for the function called upon collision with the landscape. Also see collision checking.
particle.face: Target rectangle for the graphics within Graphics.png. See particle graphics.
particle.yOff: Upper spatial limit for the particle. At this limit the particles will be deleted as if the landscape would end here. Only StdExec.
particle.delay: Delay between two animation phases. If Delay = 0 one randomly chosen phase is permanently displayed.
particle.repeats: Number of animation runs until the particle is destroyed.
particle.reverse: 0 or 1. If 1 every seconds animation is played backwards.
particle.fadeOutLen: If specified, this number of animation phases is truncated from the end and reserved for a death animation which is displayed after all repetitions of the standard animation.
particle.fadeOutDelay: Delay between two animation phases of the death animation.
particle.rByV: 0 to 3. 0 for no particle rotation. If 1 the particle will be aligned to its direction of travel; the particle's up-side will be in front. If 2 the speed parameters only determine rotation; the particle will not move. If 3 a random rotation is applied (from 4.9.8.0).
particle.gravityAcc: Effects of gravity. At 0 the particle is not affected by gravity, at 100 it is fully affected. Negative values are also possible.
particle.windDrift: Horizontal drift by wind. Same as the material property of the same name. Since CR 4.9.8.4.
particle.vertexCount: 0 or 1. If 1, collision detection is done.
particle.vertexY: Y offset of the collision checking point in percent. Also see collision detection.
particle.additive: 0 or 1. If 1, the particle is drawn additively.
particle.alphaFade: 0 to 40. Rate of fade out per frame. A fully faded particle is removed.
particle.parallaxity: Parallaxity in x and y directions. 0 is locked with the viewport; 100 is default (locked with the landscape).
particle.attach: 0 or 1. If 1 the particle is moving relative to its target object's position. From CE 4.95.4.
